chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The young girl is not consulted for marriage if she is between her two parents, for she has no authority alongside the father.
And he (peace be upon him) said: Everyone else may consult her, except the father.
ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to decide a young virgin's marriage when both parents are alive?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific legal hierarchy in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the father's exclusive right of *qiwamah* (guardianship) and the general practice of seeking consent (*istish'ar*) from other relatives. It highlights that while the father's permission is obligatory for the marriage of a virgin, the mother and others are not bound by this same obligation, reflecting the nuanced application of paternal authority in marital contracts.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘The girl cannot appoint (to get her married) when she was between the two parents, there would be no command for her’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She can appoint (a guardian from people) in the absence of the father’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘A virgin girl when living with her parents cannot appoint anyone to solemnize her marriage.
In the absence of her father anyone can ask her to be appointed as her guardian.’”
